prompt_values.issue:
DataArray.integrate has a 'dim' arg, but Dataset.integrate has a 'coord' arg
This is just a minor gripe but I think it should be fixed.

The API syntax is inconsistent:
```python
ds.differentiate(coord='x')
da.differentiate(coord='x')
ds.integrate(coord='x')
da.integrate(dim='x')   # why dim??
```
It should definitely be `coord` - IMO it doesn't make sense to integrate or differentiate over a dim because a dim by definition has no information about the distance between grid points. I think because the distinction between dims and coords is one of the things that new users have to learn about, we should be strict to not confuse up the meanings in the documentation/API.

The discussion on the original PR [seems to agree](https://github.com/pydata/xarray/pull/2653#discussion_r246164990), so I think this was just an small oversight.

The only question is whether it requires a deprecation cycle?
prompt_values.plan:
# Plan

## Goal

Rename the parameter of `DataArray.integrate` from `dim` to `coord` so it matches `Dataset.integrate(coord=...)` and both `differentiate` methods, which all use `coord`.

## Repository evidence

- `xarray/core/dataarray.py:3483` — `def integrate(self, dim: Union[Hashable, Sequence[Hashable]], datetime_unit=None)`. The docstring already describes `dim` as "Coordinate(s) used for the integration," and its body forwards the value to `Dataset.integrate`:

      ds = self._to_temp_dataset().integrate(dim, datetime_unit)

- `xarray/core/dataset.py:5966` — `def integrate(self, coord, datetime_unit=None)`, and `differentiate` on both `Dataset` (`5910`) and `DataArray` (`3424`) already use `coord`. So `DataArray.integrate` is the sole outlier.
- Every in-tree caller passes the argument positionally (`da.integrate("x")`, `da.integrate(("y","x"))`, `da.integrate("time", datetime_unit=...)`) — see `xarray/core/dataarray.py` docstring examples, `xarray/core/dataset.py` examples, `doc/computation.rst:413`, and `xarray/tests/test_dataset.py` (`test_integrate`, `test_trapz_datetime`). No code or test in the repository calls `da.integrate(dim=...)`.

## Proposed change

Edit `xarray/core/dataarray.py`:

1. Change the signature to `def integrate(self, coord: Union[Hashable, Sequence[Hashable]], datetime_unit: str = None) -> "DataArray":`.
2. Update the parameter name in the docstring (`dim` → `coord`) and reword the note ("i.e. dim must be one dimensional" → "coord"), keeping the existing cross-reference and examples.
3. Update the forwarding call to `self._to_temp_dataset().integrate(coord, datetime_unit)`.

No change is needed in `Dataset.integrate`, `differentiate`, or the underlying `_integrate_one`.

## Deprecation decision

No deprecation cycle is warranted for this change:

- The parameter is positional in all existing usage, so calls like `da.integrate("x")` keep working unchanged; only the rarely used keyword form `da.integrate(dim="x")` breaks.
- The repository has no caller using `dim=` as a keyword, so there is no internal breakage to absorb.
- The project treats this as a straight correction of an API inconsistency rather than a behavior change; a deprecation warning would add permanent keyword-handling complexity for a name that was never documented as `dim` in any correctness sense.

If the maintainers prefer an extra safety net, the alternative is to accept `dim` as a deprecated keyword alias and emit a `FutureWarning` via `xarray.core.utils.alias_warning`, but I recommend against it for the reasons above.

## Documentation

Add an entry to the unreleased `v0.17.0` section of `doc/whats-new.rst`. `DataArray.integrate` was only introduced in 0.16, so listing the rename under **Bug fixes** (next to the existing integrate doc entry around line 1056) is appropriate; if maintainers consider it API-visible, put it under **Deprecations** / **Breaking changes** instead. Suggested text:

> - Rename the `dim` argument of `DataArray.integrate` to `coord` for consistency with `Dataset.integrate` and `differentiate`.

## Tests

The existing tests already exercise the positional path and will continue to pass. To lock in the new keyword name, add a small assertion in `test_integrate` (in `xarray/tests/test_dataset.py`, near the existing `da.integrate("x")` calls), for example:

    assert_identical(da.integrate(coord="x"), da.integrate("x"))

This verifies the keyword is accepted and produces the same result as the positional form.

## Verification

Run (using the provided environment `/opt/miniconda3/envs/testbed/bin/python`):

    python -m pytest xarray/tests/test_dataset.py -k "integrate or trapz" -q

confirming both `test_integrate` and `test_trapz_datetime` pass.
